open_points.subject: M18 FlowActivation / action "activate a flow"
open_points.text: "The selection of one proven flow version as the flow's active version ... A flow's active version is the one recorded last"
open_points.question: If the requested flow version is already the active one, must the kernel write a new FlowActivation record or return the current active version without creating a record?
options: Always append a new FlowActivation record
Treat as no-op and return existing active version
open_points.default_guess: Treat as no-op and return existing active version

open_points.subject: M19 Run.status with concurrent waiting and runnable branches
open_points.text: "While some nodes wait, independent branches keep running (K-09)." and "status is `awaiting_approval` when any of them waits for the owner's approval, otherwise `pending`"
open_points.question: When a run has at least one waiting node and also still has runnable work in other branches, which single status is stored on the Run record at that moment?
options: Use waiting status (`awaiting_approval`/`pending`) as soon as any wait exists
Keep `running` until no runnable node remains, and expose waits separately
open_points.default_guess: Use waiting status as soon as any wait exists

open_points.subject: M22 SpooledFile read access vs K-14 agent disclosure rule
open_points.text: M22: "Read by ... the owner's inspection read of its bytes"; K-14: "An agent never receives a `personal_data` value ..."
open_points.question: Are agents allowed to read raw spooled file bytes when disclosure class is not `personal_data`, or are raw spool bytes owner-only regardless of class?
options: Agents may read non-`personal_data` spool bytes
Agents never read spool bytes, only metadata/digests

open_points.subject: M01 Port disclosure class on function/flow outputs
open_points.text: "A function output port carries no class ..." and "A flow output port carries no class either"
open_points.question: If an author/composer supplies `disclosure_class` on a function output port or flow output port in a request, must the kernel refuse the request or accept and ignore that field?

open_points.subject: M19 Run.waiting at terminal states
open_points.text: "`waiting`: WaitingPoints (M20) while the run waits" and final statuses include `succeeded`, `failed`, `refused`, `cancelled`
open_points.question: When a run reaches a final status (especially `cancelled` or `refused` while waits existed), must `waiting` be cleared, or may waiting points remain on the final Run record?
options: Allow terminal runs to retain last waiting points as historical snapshot
